headline: Friday was the worst day of the week: chips fell 10% to 14% into the close, the S&P 500 closed 3.7% lower in a correction, and next week brings ADI, PCE and GDP before a short holiday week.
summary: All closes here are Friday Nov 20 from Massive unless marked. The dashboard caught up: all 67 US prices we sampled match Massive, so the one day lag from Thursday is fixed. Friday morning chips were down but the S&P 500 was only about 0.2% lower early (intraday). The close was much worse: the S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39 and 8.6% for the week, its worst week since April 2025, and closed in a correction (AP; Yahoo Finance). Nvidia fell 14.01% to 125.53 after a report that the SEC is looking into its disclosures, and the chip index had its worst week since 2001. The VIX closed at 35.89 and the 10 year yield fell to about 4.91%. The WM swing setup survived (closed 239.63, over its 238.20 stop); DHR closed 220.36, under its stop, so that setup is void. Next week: ADI reports Tuesday at 7am ET, PCE, GDP, durable goods and jobless claims all land Wednesday at 8:30am ET, markets close Thursday and close at 1pm ET Friday.

regime.why: The S&P 500 fell every day this week, four times by 1% or more, which Bespoke says happened only in 1962, 1974, 1978, the week after 9/11 and October 2008 (Yahoo Finance). Bonds worked as a hedge for a second day, but gold did not. A December Fed hike is still priced at about 97.5% (CME data via Yahoo Finance).

signals.title: Friday's close: chips fell 10% to 14% and the S&P 500 and Dow closed in a correction
signals.since_yesterday: Yesterday's brief had only Friday morning: the S&P 500 about 0.2% lower early, intraday. It closed down 3.70%, and Nvidia fell 14.01% after a report of an SEC inquiry.
signals.what_happened: Closes from Massive: NVDA 125.53 (-14.01%), AMD 424.39 (-13.25%), AVGO 304.41 (-12.19%), MU 594.51 (-13.89%), TSM 318.71 (-9.48%), ANET 167.62 (-11.59%), ENTG 124.53 (-9.85%), ADI 345.92 (-8.35% on 10.2M shares), TXN 263.75 (-7.70%). In the afternoon a report said the SEC is looking into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors (first reported by the Wall Street Journal, also Reuters; the SEC does not comment), and the stock fell further (CNBC). Nvidia has fallen seven weeks in a row, its longest run since 2008, and is down 46% over that stretch (CNBC). The S&P 500 closed 10.7% under its Oct 6 high and the Dow 10.8% under its August record, both in a correction (Yahoo Finance). All 20 chip stocks in the Nasdaq 100 are in a bear market (Yahoo Finance). What rose: UNH +2.84% to 339.85, WMT +1.52% to 127.95, PG +0.91%, COST +0.76%, DUK +0.71% and TLT +1.37% (Massive).
signals.so_what: This was no longer only a crowded trade unwinding. A legal question about the leader of the AI build out adds a risk that earnings cannot fix quickly. Who pays: chip makers and the Asian supply chain. Who gets paid: bond holders, and the steady cash flow names (utilities, staples, discount retail). Third order: the range boxes that formed after the Nov 4 to 6 drop broke down Friday in many analog and industrial chip names at once (ADI 2.71x volume, TXN 2.41x, MCHP 2.94x, STM 2.4x), plus GEV, ETN and QCOM. When many boxes from one drop date break on the same day, it is the market, not news on each company. What would make this wrong: a probe that ends quickly, or ADI on Tuesday showing industrial demand holding up.
signals.for_you: Swing: no entries this week; thin holiday volume makes the 1.5x rule hard to meet. Puts: no puts on any name that broke down Friday (ADI, TXN, MCHP, GEV, ETN, PYPL, ETR, UNP, DLR). Long term: ANET, ADI and ENTG are off the long term scan buy list; wait for a close back over each point.

signals.title: Week in review: the worst week since 2020 for the Dow and Nasdaq, and gold did not hedge
signals.what_happened: For the week the S&P 500 fell 8.6%, the Dow 8.0%, the Nasdaq Composite 10% and the Russell 2000 7.5% (AP). The S&P 500 fell all five days, with four drops of 1% or more (Yahoo Finance, citing Bespoke). The chip index fell about 17%, its worst week since the one after 9/11, and SMH fell 17.81% (Yahoo Finance; Massive). Four drivers, in order: Nvidia's beat did not hold and its stock fell every day, ending with the SEC report; the US chip remote access rule took effect Nov 19; Anthropic's $81.3 billion IPO pulled money out of other AI stocks and then fell itself, closing 88.91 Friday, just above its $83 offer (Yahoo Finance); and the CMS proposal to audit Medicare Advantage plans hit insurers early in the week. Under it all, the Fed is still expected to hike in December. What held: TLT rose 2.61% and the 10 year yield fell from 5.15% to about 4.91%; DUK rose 0.48% and ORLY 0.50%; WMT (-0.11%) and COST (-0.37%) were flat (Massive). What did not hold: gold, with GLD down 9.17% (Massive).
signals.so_what: The hiding places were bonds and businesses that sell everyday things. Gold falling with stocks says some of the selling was forced: funds sold what they could, not what they wanted to. That kind of selling can end suddenly, but nothing in Friday's close says it has ended.
signals.for_you: Swing: the week cost the list three setups (MO and TMO earlier, DHR Friday); WM is the only one left. Puts: the defensive names that held (DUK, SO near their range tops) are the only groups not falling. Long term: the buy list shrank from 13 to 9 names (see actions).

signals.title: Scorecard: how the calls did
signals.what_happened: Graded Nov 20 (site/data/scorecard.json). Swings, graded by her rule (a trigger is a close over the entry on at least 1.5x the 50 day volume; the fill is that close): 27 calls, 4 finished, 3 wins (ABBV +0.25R, LNG +0.36R, BDX +0.86R) and 1 loss (EOG -1.0R), average +0.12R, unchanged for two weeks. 20 never triggered, 2 waiting (WM; WMT from Nov 20) and 1 open: WST, filled at 416.41 on Oct 29, closed 390.30 Friday, so -0.51R. Cash secured puts: the first 10 logged ideas expired Nov 20, but the scorecard still shows all 25 as open (see the data signal). Our own check against Massive Friday closes: 4 of 10 expired out of the money and kept the premium (DAL 75, PFE 27, JPM 310, FRO 45), 6 finished in the money (BHP 82.5, HPE 55, EWZ 37, C 120, IBKR 80, EWT 100). The 3 brief ideas went 2 for 3 (PFE and JPM kept, C in the money by 7.8%). The 7 scanner ideas went 2 for 7, and 4 of the 5 misses were 16% to 25% under the strike after the premium. Long term buys: 126 calls; 55 of 124 beat SPY after 5 days (44%, average 2.52 points behind) and 47 of 110 after 20 days (43%, average 3.46 behind). Brief signals: 268 calls; 120 of 227 right after 5 days (53%) and 72 of 130 after 20 days (55%, average 1.98 points ahead). My split of the 110 long term calls with 20 day results: 35 in the AI compute or AI power maps averaged 18.52 points behind SPY and 3 beat it; the other 75 averaged 3.57 points ahead and 44 beat it. Bullish signals were right 42 of 74 times at 20 days (57%); bearish ones only 26 of 56 (46%).
signals.so_what: Small samples everywhere: 4 finished swings, 10 finished puts. None of that is proof. What works: the volume rule kept the dashboard out of 20 setups that never confirmed, and long term buys outside the AI groups are ahead of SPY. Bullish brief signals are right more often than not. What does not: long term buys inside the AI groups (now seven weeks behind, close to the two month mark), the scanner's put ideas, and bearish signals, which lagged SPY on average even in a falling market. WST shows another weak spot: it confirmed 8.6% over its 383.49 entry, so the stop sat 12% under the fill and the trade is now half a loss.
signals.for_you: One rule change to consider: hold the scanner's put ideas to the brief's put rules before they are logged (verdict Buy zone now, the group not falling, no confirmed range break down). The brief's ideas kept the premium 2 of 3 times; the scanner's 2 of 7, with large losses on the misses (BHP, HPE, EWZ, EWT were all in falling groups). Still on watch from last week: the group check on long term buys. If the AI group calls are still behind in early December, the routine says to change that rule.

signals.title: Week ahead, Nov 23 to 27: ADI Tuesday, five big reports Wednesday morning, a holiday Thursday
signals.what_happened: Monday: flash PMIs 9:45am ET (manufacturing forecast 54.5, services 55.6); HPE reports after the close. Tuesday: ADI at 7am ET with a 10am call (its guide was $4.3 billion revenue and $3.86 adjusted EPS, give or take $0.15); Conference Board confidence 10am (forecast 92.5, prior 91.7); Autodesk after the close (estimate $2.27). Wednesday at 8:30am ET: October PCE (core forecast +0.3% for the month, prior 0.3%; headline forecast 3.8% for the year, prior 3.6%), income and spending, Q3 GDP second estimate (forecast 3.4%), October durable goods (forecast +0.4%, prior +1.8%) and jobless claims (forecast 200,000, prior 203,000); new home sales 10am; a 7 year note auction at 11:30am ET. Deere reports before the open, call 10am ET. There are no Fed minutes this week: the October minutes came out Nov 18, and the next come after the Dec 8 to 9 meeting. Thursday Nov 26: closed. Friday Nov 27: stocks close at 1pm ET (options 1:15pm), and China's pause on its gallium, germanium and antimony ban to the US ends that day. No extension notice was found as of Nov 21; a broader US China truce was reported extended to Jan 10, but the metals text still names Nov 27 (Environment+Energy Leader; Fastmarkets).
signals.so_what: A core PCE print of 0.4% or more, or headline above 3.8%, would make the December hike a sure thing and push yields back up, which would take away the one hedge that worked this week. A 0.2% core print would help bonds and the defensive groups most. Second order: holiday trading is thin, so moves on Wednesday can run further than the news deserves.
signals.for_you: Swing: no entries into Wednesday's data; thin Friday volume rarely meets 1.5x. Puts: no ADI, DE or DKS puts across their reports. Long term: wait for ADI's report before any chip name. MP closed 33.95; the metals date is a reason to watch, not to buy.

cycle.quadrant: Growth slowing while inflation stays high: late overheating, leaning toward stagflation
cycle.quadrant_why: No new growth data since Thursday. The test comes Wednesday: Q3 GDP is forecast at 3.4% and headline PCE inflation at 3.8% for the year, up from 3.6% (TradingView calendar). A hot inflation print with slowing spending would move the season toward stagflation. The All Weather model is not changed.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening and late. A December hike is priced at about 97.5% (CME via Yahoo Finance), and Fed Governor Cook said waiting risks falling behind the curve. Bonds rallied anyway as stocks fell: the 10 year fell from 5.15% to about 4.91% in a week.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Yields near 5% on the 10 year keep the cost of government and corporate debt high, and the AI build out leaned on borrowed money; IBD and Yahoo both name AI financing fears in this week's drop.
cycle.big_cycle: Technology and internal order. The leader of the AI build out now faces a reported SEC inquiry and lost its founder CEO on Nov 12. The midterm result added political pressure on data centers (IBD). External order: China's metals pause ends Nov 27 with no extension found.
tailwinds: Treasuries rallied while stocks fell, so bonds hedged again.
Utilities, staples and discount retail held up.
Oil stayed near $83, not a new shock.
headwinds: Five straight down days with four 1% drops.
A Fed hike priced for December while growth slows.
Gold fell with stocks, a sign of forced selling.

history.what: Bespoke counts only five weeks with an S&P 500 loss every day and four drops of 1% or more: 1962, 1974, 1978, September 2001 and October 2008 (Yahoo Finance, Nov 21, 2026). In 2001 and 2008 the Fed was already cutting fast, and stocks still made lower lows months later (2002 and March 2009).
history.lesson: A week this violent does not by itself mark the low. The bottom came when the selling exhausted and policy turned, not on the worst day.
